text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- As Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi gradually fills his cabinet with non-party ministers, U.S. ambassador Toomas Ilves has already been appointed foreign minister and a former economy minister, Jaak Leimann, will once again take up that post.
- The right-wing opposition parties are planning to form a shadow cabinet, Reform Party leaders said.
- The Russian population in north-east Estonia has the right to a referendum over separation from Estonia, Gennadi Zyuganov, leader of the Russian communists, said.
- Lithuanian authorities detained an Estonian vessel whose fishing licence expired on November 26.

- Estonian government approved the border agreement with Russia and authorised acting foreign minister Riivo Sinijarv to sign the document at the Lisbon summit. But the Russian leader at the border talks, Vassili Svirin, says the agreement is not ready for signing.
- New foreign minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves says in an interview he would continue the current course in foreign policy and has no intention to become involved in internal matters.

- Archbishop of the Estonian Lutheran Church signed the Porvoo declaration in London. The document joins the 50 million protestant believers of the Nordic and Baltic countries with those in Britain and Ireland.

- U.N. General Assembly stopped discussing the human rights situation in Latvia and Estonia, agreeing that the countries have no problems with the issue, which was raised by Russia in respect to the large Russian minority in the Baltics.
- Former Riigikogu speaker Ulo Nugis is trying to raise support to be elected the new leader of the Coalition Party of Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi at a congress on December 7.
- Estonian Air, owned by Maersk DSACAb.CO agreed to pay an 11 million kroon debt to Russia's Aeroflot. The Russian side had threatened to stop flights to Moscow if the debt was not paid.
